station-blue.purpose: The only blue and the only accent, day and night: every sign plate, label markers, the focus ring by day, result emphasis, the Tabletop selection. White lettering on it is about 6:1.

station-blue-deep.purpose: A sign under the pointer, pressed, open or current. Also --accent-strong by day (emphasis text, links); at night --accent-strong is white.

station-blue-soft.purpose: Faint wash behind a readout, inline code or a file drop under the pointer. Never a large fill, never the active state.

station-ring-night.purpose: The ink as a thin mark on black: focus rings, outlines, selection borders, the 3D selection ring. About 6:1 on black. By day --focus-ring is Station Blue itself.

sign-lettering.purpose: Words on a plate, a pictogram's outline and its square's border, the pressed sign's foot bar. Same in both themes.

sign-arrow-orange.purpose: The direction arrow in a sign's lower right corner (.signArrow, .toolCard__arrow, the current nav tab's down arrow). About 3:1 on the blue: a mark to see, not words to read. Same day and night. Also the Tabletop's Clear wedge tint at night (#c2410c by day).

true-black.purpose: Night page background, and --background-muted at night (identical by design).

paper-muted.purpose: The chalkboard's radial falloff and nested surfaces.

ink-panel.purpose: The nav bar and floating panels at night, with backdrop blur on the nav. Cards never take it.

ink-panel-strong.purpose: Opaque fill for inputs, nested panels and every Tabletop HUD plate.

hairline-border.purpose: The one line a card gets: between two cards, under the nav, around inputs and floating panels.

chalk-mark-day.purpose: Triplet every homepage hand-drawn stroke is mixed from, capped by --chalk-alpha (0.26 day). Filter url(#quop-graphite).

chalk-mark-night.purpose: Night chalk, capped by --chalk-alpha (0.30). Filter url(#quop-chalk).

display.purpose: One h1 per page on the homepage and section indexes, light (400) because at that size weight shouts. Homepage chapter headings stay light with it.

headline.purpose: h2s inside cards and sections, bold (700): with card frames gone the heading tells one group from the next. Tool pages set every heading 700; toolTitle is 700 clamp(1.8rem, 3.4vw, 2.5rem).

body.purpose: Running copy in Source Sans 3 (root 106.25%). Lead steps to 1.08rem, muted, 44rem measure.

label.purpose: Sign lettering, header tab text, and structural labels (kickers, cluster labels, beta badge) in --muted behind a 0.5em square --accent marker. Structure, never content (The Case Rule).

readout.purpose: Source Sans with tabular figures at 500: FITS crosshair coordinates, colorbar labels, header values, the Tabletop's lengths and key caps. Not mono. Calculator answers step up to the Result scale (800, clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3.2rem)).

code.purpose: System mono, not shipped: inline code, the Tabletop's JSON and AI brief, the plotters' typed-array inputs. Code only; measured values are Readout.

equation.purpose: EB Garamond italic, only for the hand-set equations on the homepage chalkboard. Nothing else is serif.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The Flat Sheet Rule: no card, button, input, panel or menu carries a box-shadow or hover lift. Depth belongs to the Tabletop's 3D scene.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus everywhere via :where(:focus-visible). Station Blue #1a5fb4 by day, Station Ring #4f8dd6 by night. Header items draw it inset (outline-offset: -3px).

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: Between two cards, under the nav, around inputs, flyouts and popovers. Never around a card.

shadows.name: builder-hairline
shadows.purpose: Separates an opaque Tabletop HUD plate from the 3D scene, visible on the night void.

shadows.name: sign-foot
shadows.value: linear-gradient(var(--on-accent), var(--on-accent)) center bottom 2px / calc(100% - 4px) 3px no-repeat
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: the 3px white bar along a pressed, open or active sign's foot, inset 2px. Carried as --sign-foot.

shadows.name: phosphor-glow
shadows.purpose: FITS crosshair glow only: instrument output, not chrome.

motion.name: sign-hover
motion.purpose: Header tab turning into a sign under the pointer. Plates change colour only; nothing lifts.

motion.name: row-wash
motion.purpose: Tool rows and the file drop taking their hover wash.

motion.name: chalk-write
motion.purpose: A board equation written in from the left; holds 8-13s, then fades.

motion.name: chalk-frame-draw
motion.purpose: A chalk card's wobbled frame drawn on when it scrolls into view; glyph and text follow on a 0.45s stagger. Collapsed under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: custom-md
breakpoints.purpose: Collapses the visualizer sidebar/plot layout to one column.

breakpoints.name: custom-sm-alt
breakpoints.purpose: Tool rows set the sign and its sentence side by side; FITS viewer figure/colorbar layout.

breakpoints.name: custom-sm
breakpoints.purpose: Field wrapping; chalk cards go to two columns.

breakpoints.name: chalk-cards-4
breakpoints.purpose: Chalk section cards run four across.

breakpoints.name: tailwind-sm
breakpoints.purpose: Tailwind's sm: on newer Tailwind-authored components (nav, shell). Match whichever idiom a file already uses.

components.name: Sign (buttonLink)

components.html: Open the Tabletop

components.name: Pictogram Sign (SignIcon)
components.description: A sign with its icon as a station pictogram: a white outline glyph in a 1.6em white-bordered square leading the words; icon-only signs pad the square by 0.3em; pressed signs gain the white foot bar.
components.css: .ds-sign { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5em; width: fit-content; border: 0; border-radius: var(--radius, 2px); background-color: var(--accent, #1a5fb4); color: var(--on-accent, #ffffff); font-family: var(--font-source-sans), -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; text-decoration: none; box-shadow: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-sign:hover { background-color: var(--accent-hover, #0f4690); } .ds-sign:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring, #1a5fb4); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-sign--icon { padding: 0.3em 0.9em 0.3em 0.3em; } .ds-sign--icon-only { padding: 0.3em; } .ds-sign.is-pressed { background: linear-gradient(#ffffff, #ffffff) center bottom 2px / calc(100% - 4px) 3px no-repeat; background-color: var(--accent-hover, #0f4690); } .ds-sign-icon { display: inline-grid; flex: none; place-items: center; width: 1.6em; height: 1.6em; border: 1.5px solid currentColor; border-radius: var(--radius, 2px); } .ds-sign-icon svg { width: 60%; height: 60%; overflow: visible; } .ds-sign-icon svg :is(path, circle, rect) { fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.5px; stroke-linecap: square; stroke-linejoin: miter; vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke; }

components.name: Action Grid Sign (buttonControl)

components.name: Tool Row (toolCard)

components.name: Tabletop HUD Island
components.description: The Sign Rule's scoped exception: HUD buttons are neutral opaque plates with a builder hairline at rest, a neutral wash on hover, and become Station Blue signs only when pressed, open or live. Flat, square, no shadow, no backdrop blur.

narrative.overview:
QUOP reads as a physicist's own working surface, not a software product. By day it's white paper worked over in graphite: plain white ground, hairline borders, blue annotations. By night it's the same room with the lights off and the board lit: true black, chalk-white marks, the same station blue lit as fills and rings around white words, the FITS viewers glowing with green phosphor crosshairs and readouts like an old instrument dial. Nothing here is trying to look like a SaaS dashboard; it's trying to look like a surface someone actually works on.

The homepage states that literally: a board the visitor arrives at mid-session, with equations from four domains being written and wiped behind the welcome. The rest of the site is the notebook the board's results get copied into.

The mood is inviting first, credible second. Invitation shows up in the hand-drawn marks, the unhurried writing and erasing, and controls that read at a glance as the signs of a station: square Station Blue plates with white lettering and an orange arrow pointing the way on. Credibility shows up underneath: exact values in tabular figures, uppercase structural labels, and instrument-grade FITS readouts that don't soften their numbers for anyone.
keyCharacteristics: White paper by day, black board by night: one Station Blue (#1a5fb4) ink in both, worn as fills and rings at night while the words go white
Every corner is square and hard: one radius, 2px (--radius), site-wide; 999px only for things round by meaning

Whatever can be pressed is a station sign: a square blue plate with white lettering, an orange arrow (#fb8c4a) in its lower right corner, and any icon a white-outlined pictogram in a white-bordered square
Cards have no frame: no border, no shadow, no fill; two cards are told apart by one thin gray hairline
The interface is flat; depth belongs to the Tabletop's 3D scene
Uppercase, letter-spaced labels mark structure and category, behind a small square accent marker; regular-case text is always content
FITS/data-instrument surfaces speak in tabular figures and green-phosphor highlights, deliberately more instrument than the chrome
Hand-drawn marks (wobbled frames, chalk strokes, italic serif equations) belong to the homepage board and nowhere else

rules.name: The Day/Night Ink Rule
rules.body: One hue in both themes. Fills are unchanged: a plate is #1a5fb4 day and night with white lettering. Thin marks lift at night to Station Ring (~#4f8dd6, --focus-ring). Words are never blue at night: --accent-text and --accent-strong go white and take emphasis from size and weight. By day, blue text stays (--accent-strong #0f4690).

rules.name: The Sign Rule
rules.body: Whatever can be pressed is a sign: an --accent plate, no border, no shadow, radius --radius, --on-accent lettering at the Label step. Hover deepens to --accent-hover; pressed/open/active keeps the deep plate and gains the 3px white foot bar (--sign-foot); disabled drops to 40% opacity, never gray; focus is the 2px ring offset 2px. The orange arrow (#fb8c4a) always sits in the lower right corner and never leads the words. The selectors live in one list at the end of globals.css. Header tabs are plates only on hover or when current (current: deep plate plus a small orange down arrow); the Tabletop HUD and the chalk cards are the scoped exceptions.

rules.name: The Pictogram Rule
rules.body: An icon on a sign is a white outline glyph (1.5px non-scaling stroke, square caps, mitred joins, never filled) inside a 1.6em white-bordered square (1.5px, radius --radius), leading the words by 0.5em. Icon-only signs pad the square by 0.3em. One component, SignIcon, whose .signIcon CSS strips fills; tool pictograms live in tool-pictograms.tsx.

rules.name: The Case Rule
rules.body: Uppercase + letter-spacing means structure/category, never body content. Something the user typed or a real physical quantity is sentence case and proportional type; a label the interface asserts is uppercase and tracked.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: No card, button, input, panel or menu carries a box-shadow or a hover lift. Floating surfaces are separated by an opaque or blurred fill and a 1px hairline. Depth is reserved for the Tabletop's lit 3D scene.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: A card has no border, shadow, fill or radius and pads 1.3rem top and bottom only. One 1px --border hairline runs between two cards, never around one, nothing above the first or below the last. Tool rows are the exception: their signs separate themselves.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: One radius, 2px (--radius, which --builder-radius follows), for every button, sign, pictogram square, card, input, menu, popover, badge, tooltip, chart frame and toast. 999px only for things round by meaning: colour dots, swatches and pickers, radio dots, wheel and fan ring geometry, round 3D parts. Tailwind rounded-* utilities are a bug here.

rules.name: The Minimal HUD Rule
rules.body: The Tabletop HUD shows only what is needed at rest, eleven controls, with related controls behind one button each. Its buttons are neutral opaque plates at rest and become signs only when pressed, open or live; hovers are a neutral wash (--builder-hover), never --accent-soft.

rules.name: The Quiet Centre Rule
rules.body: The chalk layer is masked by a radial gradient so marks dissolve before reaching the welcome text. New equation slots respect the mask; never solve an overlap by moving the welcome copy.

dos: Do keep one Station Blue ink in both themes: fills unchanged, thin marks lifted to the Station Ring, words white at night (The Day/Night Ink Rule).
Do cut every corner square: --radius (2px) everywhere, 999px only for things round by meaning (The Square Rule).

Do make whatever can be pressed a sign, through the one selector list in globals.css, with the orange arrow in the lower right corner and icons as SignIcon pictograms (The Sign Rule, The Pictogram Rule).
Do separate two cards with one thin gray hairline and nothing else (The Hairline Rule).
Do keep hand-drawn texture, chalk filters and the serif italic on the homepage board alone.
Do reserve uppercase, tracked type for structural labels behind the square accent marker, and keep real content sentence case (The Case Rule).
Do route FITS/data-instrument surfaces through tabular figures and the green-phosphor language, and keep mono for code alone.
donts: Don't treat TransitionProvider, NavTransitionLink, WavefunctionBanner, or the orbitalPhase and accent fields on navSections as part of the live design system: they are unwired dead code.
Don't introduce a second blue or any other accent hue; Station Blue and Station Blue Deep are the ink, and the orange is only ever the sign's arrow.
Don't give a card a border, fill, shadow or radius beyond --radius, or a button a shadow or a hover lift (The Flat Sheet Rule, The Hairline Rule).
Don't put a plate on anything that can't be pressed; a label, tag or badge wears the small square marker instead.
Don't fill a pictogram or round its square.
Don't use a gray or metal button; a control that can't be pressed right now is a blue sign at 40%.
Don't raise --chalk-alpha until the marks read as confidently as interface text.
